newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Aluminium to test support, copper steady.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aluminium to test support, copper steady.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper should consolidate in a range above $2,500, with a breach of $2,550 necessary for more upside momentum, analysts said.
Aluminium was under pressure and expected to test support at $1,610, they added.
COPPER -
The market should move sideways between support at $2,500 and recent highs around $2,540 after finding good buying underneath the market on recent dips.
The 10-day moving average at $2,502 should reinforce the floor, chartists said.
"Look for further consolidation...though with the technical indicators maintaining their upward bias, we continue to favour further strength," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.
The market would have to clear Wednesday's high of $2,540 and then $2,550 to keep up momentum, analysts said.
"The market is starting to look a bit tired at the highs," said broker Brandeis in a commentary.
The 14-day RSI was at 76 at Thursday's close, which indicated an overbought market but was off the peak around 80 seen last week.
At 0755 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,524/28, down about $6 from Thursday's late close.
ALUMINIUM -
The market was soggy after closing on Thursday just under its 30-day and 100-day moving averages.
"Aluminium closed below Wednesday's low...suggesting a test of $1,610 and possibly trendline support at $1,602," said chartist Harry Creates of broker AMT.
If prices sliced through $1,610, last Friday's low, and also broke below $1,607, this would confirm a head and shoulders pattern and target the February low of $1,534, Squires said.
Brandeis said a triple top seemed to be forming.
On the upside, resistance was pegged at $1,630, $1,645, and $1,659.
At 0755 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,614/17, down $8 from Thursday's late close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
